key_insight: Diffusion-Proof shows that diffusion language models can improve formal theorem proving by generating or correcting proofs with stronger long-range coherence than auto-regressive models.
engineering_relevance: It suggests a practical new model class for theorem provers, especially where proof-length, consistency, and local repair are bottlenecks.
method: Train dLLM-Prover-7B for whole-proof generation with iterative denoising over multi-token blocks.
Train dLLM-Corrector-7B for local proof repair using bidirectional in-filling and context-aware correction.
Apply diffusion-based inference to reduce error accumulation and improve tactic coherence across long proofs.
evidence_signal: Across ProofNet-Test and MiniF2F-Test, the framework outperformed an AR baseline by 1.61% and 6.14% absolute accuracy, and it solved one IMO problem missed by DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B.
watch_item: Diffusion-based proving may require careful tuning of denoising/block size and may be more computationally expensive than standard next-token decoding.
paper_title: Diffusion-Proof: Recipe for Formal Theorem Proving Beyond Auto-Regressive Generation
